title: Detroit: seeing Chick Webb, Duke Ellington and visiting bands
summary: He first hears Chick Webb and sees Ellington's band close up; touring bands played the Fox Theater and shows were the norm.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Then in Detroit is where I heard for the first time Chick Webb. In Detroit. I knew the name, you know what I mean. And then I had an opportunity to see Duke Ellington close up and to see Johnny Hodges and Sonny Greer. Sonny Greer was next in line as far as popularity. Then you had Tizol. You had Tricky Sam Nanton and you had Wellman Braud and...who else did you have?
Oh, Lawrence Brown. No, Lawrence Brown wasn't there.
Yeah. But...'cause I knew Lawrence Brown's name from Paul Howard's Quality Seranaders in California. That's the band I think that Lionel Hampton played with, too. But...
So a lot of bands came through...

A lot of bands came through Detroit and played the Fox Theater. You see, again I said, shows were factors. Shows were the principal items and the musicians...Of course, they would begin that transition period of...from shows to just having...they'd have like a vaudeville--five acts--and maybe the principal act would be the band. Duke and Lucky Millinder and Cab Calloway and, of course, Count Basie hadn't left Kansas City then. He didn't leave Kansas City until...
Oh yes, '36. Yeah, well, I guess he had left Kansas
City and ventured on . But Bennie Moten, I understand, had been up this way and played the Pearl Theater in Philadelphia or the 'Standard, or one of those theaters
